book.progress: The fifty are being chosen slowly and thoughtfully. A little more than half already have their place.

funny.label: Funny Harlan Stories
funny.description: The stories that made everyone laugh, and a few that still do.
funny.journeyIntro: Some of what a person leaves behind is simply the way they made a room feel lighter. These are the Fridays that begin with a straight face and end with the whole table laughing.

grief.label: Grief and Memory
grief.description: What remains after someone is gone — and how the remembering keeps going.
grief.journeyIntro: This is the quietest part of the archive. Not the ending, but everything that keeps on after one — the chair no one could sit in, and the Fridays that kept coming anyway.

momdad.label: Mom and Dad Stories
momdad.description: The people he came from, and the home they made together.
momdad.journeyIntro: Every family has a centre of gravity. Walk into the rooms Harlan grew up in and later kept — the parents, the chair, the ordinary devotions that hold a family together.

toledo.label: Toledo Childhood
toledo.description: Growing up in Toledo — the streets, the small adventures, the beginning of everything.
toledo.journeyIntro: Before he was anyone's father, brother or husband, he was a boy in Toledo. This is where the whole life starts — dimes, balconies, and afternoons that felt endless.

shabbat.label: Jewish Life / Shabbat
shabbat.description: Shabbat kept most Fridays — sometimes imperfectly, always on purpose.
shabbat.journeyIntro: Faith here is less a doctrine than a rhythm: candles, a table, a week set down gently. Follow the traditions that returned every Friday, whatever else the year had done.

ordinary.label: Ordinary Moments
ordinary.description: The small, unremarkable things that turned out to hold a whole life.
ordinary.journeyIntro: The umbrella that never opened. The things that rode along for decades, unremarked. These are the memories made of nothing much — which is exactly why they lasted.

featuredQuote.cite: — Harlan, as remembered by his brother
featuredQuote.text: You don't have to win every argument, Hal. Sometimes you just let your mother be right, and you both get to eat dinner in peace.
